A total of 21 trials involving 7908 patients were included.

articles.title: Open Visiting Policy and Delirium in Adult Patients in ICUs: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Clinical Trials.
articles.summary: To critically evaluate the comparative effects of open or flexible family presence policies vs. restricted or traditional family presence policies on the occurrence of delirium and other major outcomes among adult patients admitted to ICUs. We included randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing open or flexible vs. restricted ICU visiting policies in adult patients. Thirteen RCTs comprising 3861 patients were included. Random-effects models showed that compared with restricted policies, open/flexible family presence reduced delirium occurrence (risk ratio [RR], 0.48; 95% CI, 0.29-0.81; low certainty) and IMV duration (mean difference [MD], -0.36 d; 95% CI, -0.46 to -0.26 d; low certainty). The intervention did not affect the ICU length of stay (MD, 4.21 d; 95% CI, -4.65 to 13.07 d; very low certainty), the rates of hospital-acquired infections (RR, 1.00; 95% CI, 0.81-1.23; low certainty), or ICU mortality (RR, 0.88; 95% CI, 0.72-1.08; very low certainty).

articles.title: Comparative efficacy and safety of hydrocortisone-based regimens in septic shock: A network meta-analysis.
articles.summary: We conducted a PRISMA-compliant systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials evaluating hydrocortisone and/or fludrocortisone in adults with septic shock (PubMed, Embase, CENTRAL; inception-May 1, 2025; PROSPERO CRD420251015672). A total of 21 trials involving 7908 patients were included. Hydrocortisone ≥300 mg/day and hydrocortisone 200-299 mg/day combined with fludrocortisone 50 μg/day were associated with reduced 28-day mortality compared with placebo (OR 0.53, 95% CI 0.29-0.96; OR 0.78, 95% CI 0.64-0.96, respectively), with higher fludrocortisone doses showing numerically greater point estimates of benefit, though estimates were not statistically significant. The optimal corticosteroid regimen for septic shock, particularly the dosing and combination of hydrocortisone and fludrocortisone, remains uncertain due to inconsistent mortality findings across trials. Interventions were grouped into six regimens (including placebo), and outcomes were analyzed using a frequentist random-effects model; the primary outcome was 28-day mortality.
